newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU moves to crack down on designer drugs.
newsitem.headline: EU moves to crack down on designer drugs.

text.p: European Union justice ministers said they had made progress on Monday on a system to plug loopholes which make it easy to make and sell so-called designer drugs like ecstasy in the EU market.

Under the system, which has still to be firmed up, EU countries would create an early warning system and improve exchanges of information on new types of drugs, increasingly made in non-EU eastern European states where the lists of banned products are laxer and production cheaper.
"What's happening is that the production has moved from Holland or Belgium to the Czech Republic or Poland," the EU's Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin told reporters.
As things stand, clandestine producers can run rings round lists of banned products by slightly changing the chemical make-up of the drugs.

According to the plan, EU members would have to send detailed information on the production, trafficking and use of new synthetic drugs to the drugs unit of the EU police agency Europol and the bloc's drugs monitoring unit in Lisbon.
If the EU's experts during a risk assessment find a substance is dangerous the EU ministers can agree to put it on the banned list and EU governments will have to comply.
